title: Beatrix and the Verdict
premise: August Voss, the concierge of the Meridian Hotel, is hired by a guest to find her sister Beatrix, a tide-pool researcher who vanished three weeks ago. The case seems closed when Beatrix's diary washes ashore — until August realizes entries continue past the date of her disappearance, written in a hand that isn't quite hers. Following the diary's coded references to hotel guests and staff, August discovers Beatrix was alive for days after vanishing, hiding inside the Meridian itself while documenting who was hunting her. The trail leads to the one person August trusted most — their mentor, the head concierge, who killed Beatrix to bury an old crime she'd uncovered. In a final confrontation on the tidal flats at low water, August forces a confession recorded in the diary's own ink, choosing truth over loyalty as the tide comes in.
about_author: V. M. Sandoval spent a decade working night desks at grand coastal hotels, collecting the small betrayals and quiet heroics of people far from home. They write mysteries about observers — those paid to notice everything and forbidden to say it aloud.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Waited
chapters.summary: POV: August Voss. A rain-soaked woman named Ilse checks into the Meridian and asks August to find her missing sister, Beatrix, a marine researcher last seen near the hotel. August, who prides themselves on closing every case they accept, takes it against their better judgment. Emotional beat: the itch of curiosity overriding professional caution.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: POV: August. Police find Beatrix's diary washed up on the flats; the case is ruled accidental drowning. But August notices the final entries are dated nine days after her disappearance, and the handwriting degrades into something forced. Emotional beat: unease hardening into certainty that everyone else wants to ignore.

chapters.title: Entries in Another Hand
chapters.summary: POV: August, with flashbacks from Beatrix's diary itself. The late entries use the hotel's private shorthand — room numbers, service codes only staff would know. Beatrix was alive, hiding somewhere in the Meridian, writing in code. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt tangled with dread at what she was hiding from.

chapters.title: Room 412 Never Slept
chapters.summary: POV: August. Reconstructing the diary's codes, August traces Beatrix's movements through the hotel: the laundry chute, the old service elevator, an unused fourth-floor room. Someone has quietly erased the evidence — fresh paint, replaced linens. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing the killer is inside the building, and inside the staff.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: August. August's mentor, Edmund Hale, head concierge for thirty years, begins asking pointed questions about the diary. August lies to him for the first time. Flashback reveals Hale taught August everything about noticing. Emotional beat: the first crack in loyalty — guilt sharpened by affection.

chapters.title: Ilse's Half of the Story
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse. Ilse confesses the sisters hadn't spoken in years; Beatrix had been investigating a death at the Meridian decades ago — a maid who fell from the roof, ruled suicide. Ilse came not just to search but to finish what Beatrix started. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance; two strangers bound by someone lost.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Silence
chapters.summary: POV: alternating August and diary entries. The decoded entries reveal Beatrix's nine hidden days: she witnessed Hale meeting someone from his past, realized he'd staged the maid's death long ago, and hid rather than run. Her last entry names no one — but describes hands August knows intimately. Emotional beat: horror arriving slowly, like cold water rising.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Lobby
chapters.summary: POV: August. August plants a false lead — a fabricated diary page 'found' implicating a retired bellhop — and watches who moves to destroy it. Only one person accesses the back office overnight: Hale. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of proof, and the loneliness of knowing you're right about someone you love.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: POV: August. August lures Hale to the tidal flats with the real diary, threatening exposure. Hale admits everything — the maid knew his secret, Beatrix knew the maid's secret — and moves toward violence as the tide turns. August's recorder runs in a waterproof case beside Beatrix's own buried notes. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve; the moment of choice between silence and truth.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Missing
chapters.summary: POV: August, coda from Ilse. Hale is arrested; the maid's case is reopened and her name restored to the hotel's history wall. August returns the completed diary to Ilse and, for the first time, declines to take a new case — choosing instead to stay and remember. Emotional beat: mourning braided with belonging; truth kept as an act of loyalty to the dead.
